Variants.Content: The Mander and its many tributaries course through the fertile plains of the Reach, flowing past Highgarden before emptying into the Sunset Sea toward the Shield Islands. Its network of waters irrigates grainfields, orchards, and vineyards, turns millwheels, and lets grain, timber, wine casks, and soldiers move along the river. The abundance of the Reach comes not from soil alone, but from cheap water transport that carries the produce of manors to markets and ports. Bridges, fords, and river ports thus carry political weight; floods, silting, or an enemy blockade of a single stretch of channel can shift grain prices far away. The Mander nourishes all the daily labor behind the songs of chivalry.

Farmers of the Reach judge irrigation by the color of the Mander's water, while boatmen load cargo by the shallows and the span of bridge arches. Nobles praise the golden fields; working folk know better how much mud, water, and aching shoulders every sack of grain passes through first.

Magnates of the Reach treat river ports, mills, and bridge tolls as steady revenue, yet must keep exactions from choking off trade. River water flows around stones, and trade routes likewise bend around overly greedy tollgates.

Looking up the Mander from its mouth, the ironborn see both a waterway into a rich heartland and the defensive line of the Shield Islands. Folk of the Reach call the river a mother; raiders see every granary along its banks as a prize.
